one_liner: Adobe's ecommerce platform (Magento) for building and running online stores

evidence.claim: Official docs list token-based, OAuth-based, and session-based authentication for the web APIs
Session-based authentication is also a documented auth option
Integration OAuth credentials are created by the store admin; the integration OAuth flow is OAuth 1.0a-style
evidence.quote: I've created an integration on adobe admin. I have taken these secrets to postman and would like to now auth with OAuth 1.0

evidence.claim: Documented REST APIs cover both Adobe Commerce PaaS and the SaaS cloud service, with separate PaaS and SaaS references
evidence.quote: The REST API documentation describes the REST APIs that are available in Adobe Commerce (PaaS) and Adobe Commerce as a Cloud Service (SaaS).

evidence.claim: A full GraphQL API is offered alongside REST, plus legacy SOAP services
evidence.quote: The API is organized around a single GraphQL endpoint that provides access to the full range of Adobe Commerce and Magento Open Source features.

notes: Credentials are per-store: a merchant admin creates an integration in the Magento Admin (or uses admin/customer token auth); there is no central Adobe-issued API key for storefront data. Integration OAuth is OAuth 1.0a (per community report), not OAuth 2.0. SOAP is legacy ('Use SOAP services' still documented). A community MCP server exists (github.com/rafaelstz/adobe-commerce-dev-mcp, listed on mcp.so) but is NOT vendor-official. Docs split into PaaS vs SaaS (Commerce as a Cloud Service) references, so endpoint surface differs by deployment.
